Definition: from G5259 and G2736; down under, i.e. beneath:--under.
BiblicalUsage: In the New Testament, hypokátō is the word for down under, beneath. It appears in Matthew and Mark, and each time it carries that same plain sense.
TheologicalSignificance: For me, hypokátō means down under, beneath, nothing more and nothing less.
RelatedTopics: Word of God; Faith; Christian Life
